indicator_label: Case infrastructure keeps clearing cleanly, but the DLA/government dispute just got a lot bigger in dollar terms
summary: October 13 was a heavy filing day (20 new docket entries, all substantive or near-substantive) but most of it was case plumbing falling into place without friction: the bar date order was entered exactly as proposed (Nov 16, 2026 general / Feb 26, 2027 governmental, no objections), and both the Cole Schotz co-counsel and Verita Global administrative-advisor retention orders were entered with zero objections. The Kirkland & Ellis lead-counsel and Portage Point/CTO retentions are one step from final entry, each needing only a supplemental declaration and certification of counsel this period. The real news, however, came from the United States: in a motion seeking adequate protection of its setoff rights ahead of the November 16 sale hearing, the government disclosed that two previously-sealed False Claims Act qui tam suits against Noble have now been partially unsealed, and that it values its total damages/penalties claim in those suits at no less than $266 million — roughly 30 times the ~$8 million that has been the public face of the DLA dispute until now. The same filing confirmed the government is formally refusing to consent to the assumption of 100+ federal contracts at the Debtors' proposed $0 cure cost, and DLA separately moved to lift the stay to terminate ~21,000 largely-dead delivery orders. A vendor (Anduril Industries) also surfaced an objection showing its $27 million DLA-linked purchase order was omitted entirely from the cure-cost notice — a reminder that more such gaps could appear as other counterparties review that notice. None of this changes the sale timeline on its face, but it meaningfully raises the stakes around how much of any sale proceeds the government will seek to have reserved, and adds a second major open dispute (on top of the still-undesignated stalking horse) to watch heading into the October 16 final cash collateral hearing and the October 28 hearing on these new DLA/government motions.

indicator_label: First full-month financials land; Debtors push back hard on the $266M government claim
summary: A large batch of 19 new filings landed on October 21, dominated by two developments. First, the first full-month Monthly Operating Reports (for September 2026) were filed for all eleven debtors — only the lead debtor (Noble Supply & Logistics), K.D. Analytical Consulting, and holding company Noble.com reported actual activity; the other eight remain shell-like with $0 across the board. The lead debtor's operations were roughly breakeven ($378K gross profit on $17.7M revenue) with a net cash increase of $9.2M for the month (helped by a $15M AR collection and a voluntary $2M paydown of the Blue Torch term loan), though a $7.0M net loss on paper (mostly interest expense) continues to erode book equity. Second, the Debtors filed forceful objections to both pending government motions: a limited objection to DLA's stay-relief motion (seeking to exclude already-completed, already-paid delivery orders from termination) and a full objection asking the court to flatly deny the government's $266 million adequate-protection request, arguing it's an improper re-litigation of a ruling the court already made and that the government's sole evidentiary support — a thin attorney declaration — is inadmissible. The Committee of Unsecured Creditors reserved its rights on both motions rather than taking a side. No stalking horse bidder has been designated, and that deadline (October 23) is now imminent.

indicator_label: Mixed but net-positive week: major legal risk cleared, sale enters its final stretch with no stalking horse
summary: Two major, previously-open threats resolved this week, and the sale process reached its most consequential milestone yet. The bankruptcy court denied the government's bid for adequate-protection priority over its $1 billion-plus FCA/qui tam claims — a significant win that keeps those disputed claims from jumping ahead of other creditors in the sale-proceeds waterfall, at least for now. In the same ruling, the court let DLA move forward with terminating ~21,000 dead delivery orders (a formality with little practical effect, since most of the underlying contracts had already expired or been non-renewed) and ordered the government to pay Noble $8.49 million on undisputed invoices by November 9. Separately, the Notice of Auction confirms more than one Qualified Bid was received by the October 30 deadline, so the long-anticipated Auction will proceed on November 4 — but still with no stalking horse ever having been designated, which keeps the eventual sale price less certain than a typical process.
